season_loss_cost_note: Share of maximum exposure paid out in the 2023 season. NOT a rate on line: one season is one observation, and 2023 was exceptional. No frequency estimate exists for this POC.
calibration_status: Calibrated on the gridded index (2026-09-01). Attachment 110 km/h is a damage-onset threshold; the second tier at 125 is separated by 15 km/h, wider than the maximum measured model-to-station gap (13.7), so the two tiers are distinguishable by weather rather than by model error. Two tiers only: the index ceilings at 130.9, leaving 20.9 km/h above attachment, and a third tier would need boundaries finer than the hazard's own error. Thresholds are calibrated on THIS index and are not point-gust damage thresholds; a station-triggered live product needs its own calibration. Frequency is still one season, so the cost below is not a premium.
source_caveat: ERA5 reanalysis: backtest and pricing only. A live product would trigger on station gusts (MetService AWS), never on this.
index_caveat: Peak gust during the season's analysed cyclone events, NOT an annual maximum. 28 km grid cells, so exposed sites read higher than shown.
index_ceiling_note: Highest value the gridded index reaches anywhere in the analysed season. Point observations exceed it (MetService recorded 159.3 km/h at Channel Island in Gabrielle vs 131 here): a 28 km cell cannot resolve a headland. Any payout threshold above this ceiling can never trigger.

prediction.reason: no observed NZ cyclone loss series exists; not fabricated

hazard.note: Modelled ERA5 cell gust minus measured aerodrome gust. Conflates model error with exposure difference; aerodromes are a floor on the regional peak.
